walkthroughs.body_html:
Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report — a core area of Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which statistical test compares observed with expected frequencies?
options: Chi-squared
Spearman's rank
Standard deviation
The mean

mcqs.q: Spearman's rank is used to test what?
options: The strength of correlation between two ranked variables
The difference between two maps
The discharge of a river
The age of rock samples

mcqs.q: What should a good fieldwork hypothesis be?
options: A clear, testable statement linking two measurable variables
A vague question with no variables
A statement of proven fact
A personal opinion about the area

mcqs.q: Which is an ethical consideration in geography fieldwork?
options: Gaining consent and avoiding harm to people and environments
Using the largest sample regardless of disturbance caused
Keeping your results secret from your teacher
Inventing data when collection is difficult

mcqs.q: Does a strong Spearman's rank correlation prove that one variable causes the other?
options: No - correlation shows association only; causation requires theory and further evidence, and a third factor may be driving both variables.
A high correlation coefficient proves causation.
You should adjust the data so the hypothesis is supported.
Spearman's rank can only be used on temperature data.

mcqs.q: Is a bigger sample always better in fieldwork?
options: You should adjust the data so the hypothesis is supported.
A sample of one site is fine if it is measured very carefully.
A larger sample reduces random error, but the sampling strategy must also be unbiased and practical; a big biased sample is still misleading.
Sample size is the only thing that matters when collecting data.

mcqs.q: If your data do not support your hypothesis, has the fieldwork failed?
options: Spearman's rank can only be used on temperature data.
No - rejecting a hypothesis is a valid scientific outcome; the report should evaluate why, considering methods, anomalies and the underlying theory.
You should adjust the data so the hypothesis is supported.
Fieldwork only succeeds if the hypothesis is confirmed.

sequence.def: Set the aim and a testable hypothesis before any fieldwork
Use sampling (random/systematic) to gather data in the field
Organise into tables, graphs and maps (e.g. choropleth)
Apply tests like Spearman's Rank to find relationships
Answer the hypothesis using the evidence gathered
Assess reliability, limitations and how to improve the study
